'''Robin Thomas''' (August 22, 1962 – March 26, 2020) was a mathematician working in [[graph theory]] at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]].

Thomas received his doctorate in 1985 from [[Charles University in Prague|Charles University]] in [[Prague]], [[Czechoslovakia]] (now the [[Czech Republic]]), under the supervision of [[Jaroslav Nešetřil]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Robin Thomas|id=44107}}.</ref> He joined the faculty at Georgia Tech in 1989, and became a Regents' Professor there,<ref>Author biography from {{cite arXiv|title=Voting in agreeable societies|first1=Deborah E.|last1=Berg|first2=Serguei|last2=Norine|first3=Francis Edward|last3=Su|first4=Robin|last4=Thomas|first5=Paul|last5=Wollan|year=2008|class=math.CO|eprint=0811.3245 }}.</ref><ref>[http://www.cc.gatech.edu/news/robin-thomas-earns-distinction-named-regents-professor Robin Thomas Earns Distinction, Named Regents' Professor] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222162453/http://www.cc.gatech.edu/news/robin-thomas-earns-distinction-named-regents-professor |date=2017-12-22 }}, Georgia Tech College of Computing, June 24, 2010.</ref>
briefly serving as the department chair.

==Personal life==
Thomas was married to Icelandic [[operations research]]er [[Sigrún Andradóttir]], also a professor at Georgia Tech.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.isye.gatech.edu/news/memoriam-robin-thomas|title=In Memoriam: Robin Thomas|date=April 22, 2020|publisher=H. Milton Stewart School of Industrial and Systems Engineering|access-date=2025-04-04}}</ref>

On March 26, 2020, he died of [[amyotrophic lateral sclerosis]] at the age of 57 after 12 years of struggle with the illness.<ref name=death>{{cite web|url=https://blog.computationalcomplexity.org/2020/03/robin-thomas.html|title=Robin Thomas|date=March 28, 2020|work=Computational Complexity|first=Lance|last=Fortnow|authorlink=Lance Fortnow}}</ref><ref>[https://math.gatech.edu/news/robin-thomas-tribute Robin Thomas tribute], Georgia Tech Mathematics, April 7, 2020.</ref>

== Awards ==
Thomas was awarded the [[Fulkerson Prize]] for outstanding papers in [[discrete mathematics]] twice:<ref>[https://www.ams.org/prizes/fulkerson-prize.html Fulkerson Prize: Official site with award details].</ref> in 1994 as co-author of a paper on the [[Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)|Hadwiger conjecture]],<ref>{{citation|title=Hadwiger's conjecture for ''K''<sub>6</sub>-free graphs|author1-link=Neil Robertson (mathematician)|last1=Robertson|first1=Neil|author2-link=Paul Seymour (mathematician)|last2=Seymour|first2= Paul|last3=Thomas|first3=Robin|journal=[[Combinatorica]]|volume=13|issue=3|year=1993|doi=10.1007/BF01202354|pages=279–361|s2cid=9608738}}.</ref> and in 2009 for the proof of the [[strong perfect graph theorem]].<ref>{{citation| first1=Maria|last1=Chudnovsky|author1-link=Maria Chudnovsky|author2-link=Neil Robertson (mathematician)|last2=Robertson|first2=Neil|author3-link=Paul Seymour (mathematician)|last3=Seymour|first3= Paul|last4=Thomas|first4=Robin| year = 2006| url = http://annals.princeton.edu/annals/2006/164-1/p02.xhtml| title = The strong perfect graph theorem| journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]]| volume = 164 | issue = 1 | doi = 10.4007/annals.2006.164.51| pages = 51–229|arxiv=math/0212070|s2cid=119151552}}.</ref>
In 2011, he was awarded the [[Karel Janeček]] Foundation Neuron Prize for Lifetime Achievement in Mathematics.<ref>[http://www.nfkj.cz/cena-neuron-2011 Karel Janeček Foundation 2011 Neuron Prize winners (in Czech)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121223092613/http://www.nfkj.cz/cena-neuron-2011 |date=2012-12-23 }}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-08-27.</ref>
He was named a [[SIAM Fellow]] in 2018.<ref>{{citation|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2018-fellows|title=SIAM Announces Class of 2018 Fellows|magazine=SIAM News|date=March 29, 2018}}</ref>  The January 2023 issue of the [[Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B]] was a tribute to his work.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/j.jctb.2022.10.001|title=Editorial {{!}} Robin Thomas (1962–2020)|last1=Krivelevich|first1=Michael|author-link=Michael Krivelevich|last2=Mohar|first2=Bojan|date=2023|journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B}} </ref>
